skill.name: supabase
skill.description: Navigate Supabase database tables, relationships, query patterns, and MCP access for the Empathy Ledger project.
skill.summary: Map Supabase schema relationships and query patterns for Empathy Ledger data work.
skill.author: Acurioustractor

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, table names, relative documentation links, and schema relationship examples. The confirmed risk is the hardcoded Supabase MCP access, especially the write-capable endpoint and database tools documented in SKILL.md. No prompt-injection language or hidden executable payload was found.

remediation.issue: Write-capable Supabase MCP endpoint is published in the skill.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the write-access URL or replace it with setup steps that require explicit user-provided configuration and confirmation.

remediation.issue: A project-specific Supabase MCP project reference is hardcoded.
remediation.suggestion: Use placeholders for project_ref values and keep live project identifiers in private configuration.

remediation.issue: The skill mixes many examples with scanner-sensitive Markdown syntax.
remediation.suggestion: Label examples clearly and separate operational commands from static reference tables to reduce false-positive audit noise.

static_findings.snippet: > Use `npx supabase gen types typescript --local` to generate accurate types.
stories.storyteller_id  → profiles.id       // Who told this story
stories.project_id      → projects.id       // Which project it belongs to
stories.organization_id → organisations.id  // Which org owns it
// Note: stories can link to transcripts via content or transcript_id
tenants.organization_id        → organisations.id  // Primary org for tenant
story_access_tokens.story_id     → stories.id  // Which story (ephemeral share links)
story_access_tokens.created_by   → profiles.id // Who created the link
**IMPORTANT**: Always filter by tenant_id for data isolation.

content.value_statement: Supabase projects can be hard to query when tables, types, and relationships drift. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused schema context and query patterns.
actual_capabilities: Maps Empathy Ledger Supabase tables, views, and foreign-key relationships.
Shows query patterns for stories, transcripts, organisations, media, and share tokens.
Explains browser, server, and service-role Supabase client usage.
Highlights tenant_id filtering for safer multi-tenant data access.
Points to migration files and TypeScript type files by domain.
Documents Supabase MCP access details included in the skill.
limitations: It is project-specific and does not discover arbitrary Supabase schemas.
It cannot verify live schema drift without configured Supabase or MCP access.
Write-capable MCP references require operator review before use.
Examples are guidance and are not tested production migrations.

use_cases.title: Plan Feature Queries
use_cases.description: Find the right tables and joins before building story, media, or organisation features.

use_cases.title: Audit Schema Drift
use_cases.description: Compare live Supabase objects, migrations, and TypeScript coverage to identify maintenance gaps.

use_cases.title: Debug Tenant Data
use_cases.description: Trace tenant-scoped records, share tokens, and distribution tables while respecting isolation rules.

prompt_templates.title: Find Core Tables
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me which Supabase tables store stories, transcripts, media, organisations, and tenants. Explain the key relationships in simple terms.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Safe Query
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a Supabase query for published stories with storyteller and project details. Include tenant filtering and explain each relationship.

prompt_templates.title: Check Type Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the migration-defined tables with the TypeScript type files described by this skill. List drift that could affect story distribution features.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Read-Only Investigation
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a read-only Supabase MCP investigation for story_access_tokens, embed_tokens, and audit_logs. Avoid writes and state what evidence to collect.

output_examples.input: Where do story cards get storyteller profile data?
output_examples.output: Use stories joined through storyteller_id to profiles. Include tenant filtering and add project or media joins only when the UI needs them.

output_examples.input: Why is an embedded story not loading?
output: Check the story distribution status and related embed token.
Verify the story id, distribution id, allowed domain, and revocation state.
Review audit or access logs with read-only access first.

output_examples.input: Which files define database types for content work?
output_examples.output: Start with the content-media, story-ownership, story-access-tokens, and cultural-sensitivity type files listed by the skill.

best_practices: Always include tenant_id filters when querying tenant-scoped data.
Use read-only MCP access for inspection unless a human approves writes.
Regenerate and review Supabase TypeScript types after schema changes.
anti_patterns: Do not use service-role clients in browser code.
Do not assume migration files match the live Supabase schema.
Do not run write-capable MCP operations without explicit approval.

faq.question: Is this a general Supabase skill?
faq.answer: No. It is tailored to the Empathy Ledger database schema and query patterns.

faq.question: Does it connect to Supabase automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents MCP endpoints and tools, but access still depends on the user environment.

faq.question: Can it write database changes?
faq.answer: The skill references write-capable MCP access. Use read-only access unless a human approves writes.

faq.question: Does it replace generated TypeScript types?
faq.answer: No. It points to type files and recommends regenerating types when the live schema changes.

faq.question: What data domains does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers identity, projects, stories, media, distribution, analytics, safety, and administration tables.

faq.question: How should Claude Code or Codex use it?
faq.answer: Use it as schema context before writing queries, debugging joins, or planning read-only database checks.
